findings: Scope (S10): the diff from setup commit 62f98b3 to HEAD touches only blender/build_patch_one.py, src/patch-one-glb.js, src/take-apart-client.js, scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs, tests/take-apart.test.js, tests/web-render-finish.test.js, evidence/ and runs/wo-gh-14/. There are no changes to vendored three.js, page chrome, the model or interaction code, or other runs' evidence. brain/decisions does not exist in this repo, so I checked against the spec and brain/project.md only.

Both sides of the problem are handled where the spec says (R4, R5). The asset change is limited to material parameters in build_patch_one.py. Silicone grain scale goes from 8 to 2 and normal strength from .65 to .85. LED emission goes from .5 to 1.4. Trace contact material becomes a metallic copper-gold. The client adds a PMREM studio environment, rebalanced lights, exposure .95, and per-material envMapIntensity, lens and silicone adjustments. Stack order, translations, layer thicknesses, footprint, wordmark and LED geometry are untouched, since only material nodes changed.

Asset budget: the builder reports the GLB at 798,088 bytes against the 819,200 limit, down 4 bytes from 798,092. The module and the Blender build logs (blender-build-1.log and blender-build-2.log) are committed for the reproducibility check. I did not re-run the Blender build.

Tests and capture script: SETUP_COMMIT is re-based to 62f98b3 in both test files, and take-apart.test.js's scope allowlist is rewritten to the S10 list. This fits the S10 allowance for scope or baseline constants re-based for this order, but the allowlist rewrite is larger than a one-constant change. The reviewer-tests station should confirm no assertion changed meaning. The capture script change is a small CAPTURE_DIR env override that leaves the default output paths unchanged. That is justified by the before/after requirement (R7), and the script still runs the bundled Worker, not the unbundled source.

Client structure: the on-load material handling stays inside the existing per-layer material clone, so material ownership per layer and the baseOpacity binding are preserved. Two fragile points, neither a blocker. The silicone onBeforeCompile patch string-replaces three.js shader chunk text ('normalScale;'), which only works while the vendored three.js bytes stay frozen as the spec requires. The source uses '\\n' escapes inside the GLSL strings. The after browser-pass.log records 0 console errors and 0 page errors with scene ready, so it works in the bundled output, but this is worth a note for any future three.js bump.

Evidence layout matches R7 and R8. Before/ and after/ each hold five beats, a contact sheet, a browser screenshot, a browser-pass.log and a bundle-build.log, and the after log shows zero errors. Whether the page rendering actually closes the shield, battery and sensor, silicone grain and LED problems is a visual judgement for reviewer-design. It is outside this architecture review, and I make no claim either way.
The builder reports the suite as green except the known S11 failure and one existing skip. I did not re-run the suite. Deployment stays out of the run, which is correct.
